rounds.text: Radhika Jeweltech Ltd trades at an attractive valuation with a price-to-earnings ratio of 9x [E1], sitting significantly below its sector benchmark P/E of 24.38x [E6]. The underlying business displays exceptional operational efficiency and profitability, highlighted by a robust return on capital employed (ROCE) of 23.01% against a sector benchmark of 10.71% [E10], alongside a median return on equity of 21% over the last year [E29]. Growth metrics further underpin the strength of the firm, demonstrating a compounded sales growth of 36% over five years [E15] and a compounded profit growth of 36% over three years [E20], outperforming sector medians [E72, E73]. Furthermore, the company maintains a conservatively financed balance sheet with a debt-to-equity ratio of just 0.13x [E37] and shrinking borrowings [E38], while operating margins have expanded by 3 percentage points over the trailing twelve months compared to three years earlier [E30]. Conceded: [E34], [E35], [E36], [E40], [E51].

Radhika Jeweltech faces significant concerns regarding its internal cash generation and capital allocation, as evidenced by a negative operating cash flow of Rs -13 Cr and a free cash flow of Rs -14 Cr in March 2026 [E35, E36]. This disconnect between reported profits and actual cash realization results in a concerning cash conversion ratio of -0.17x [E34]. Furthermore, the company offers no dividend yield to shareholders, failing to provide a tangible return despite its reported profitability [E4, E59]. Investor confidence appears to be waning, evidenced by a 6.05 percentage point reduction in promoter holdings since December 2023 and negative institutional money flow [E40, E43, E60]. The stock’s technical health is poor, as it trades below both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages with a weak relative-strength rating of 21 [E49, E50, E68]. Conceded: the company maintains strong historical growth metrics, including a 36% compounded sales growth over five years and a 23.01% ROCE [E15, E10]. However, the combination of negative cash flows, declining promoter ownership, and a 27.8% twelve-month price decline suggests that the market is currently pricing in substantial operational risks [E25, E35, E40, E51].

The bear’s focus on negative cash flow [E35, E36] ignores the company’s robust profitability and consistent margin expansion, with operating margins rising by 3 percentage points over the last three years [E30] and reaching 21% in the most recent quarter [E31]. While the cash conversion ratio is currently negative [E34], the company maintains a conservative financial structure with a debt-to-equity ratio of only 0.13x and reduced total borrowings [E37, E38]. Conceded: the company does not currently pay a dividend [E4, E59]. The decline in promoter holding [E40, E60] is offset by the fact that the business is fundamentally outperforming its sector, delivering an ROE of 20.7% and an ROCE of 25.0% [E12, E13], which significantly exceed the sector benchmarks of 8.71% and 10.71% respectively [E9, E10]. Furthermore, the market’s current technical pessimism [E49, E50] ignores the reality that the stock is trading at a P/E of 8.77x, a deep discount to the sector benchmark of 24.38x [E6]. Finally, the current price implies negative growth [E46], which is entirely disconnected from the company’s actual performance of 18% profit growth and 19% sales growth over the trailing twelve months [E17, E21].

Conceded: operating margins have expanded to 21% [E31] and the company trades at a P/E of 8.77x against a sector benchmark of 24.38x [E6]. However, the bull minimizes the severity of a negative cash conversion of -0.17x and an operating cash flow of Rs -13 Cr alongside a free cash flow of Rs -14 Cr in Mar 2026 [E34, E35, E36], indicating that robust profits are failing to materialize as actual cash. Furthermore, the bull downplays insider dilution by citing operational outperformance, yet promoter holdings have dropped by 6.05 percentage points over the last three years down to 57.68% [E40, E60], accompanied by negative institutional money flow [E43]. While the bull points to strong trailing growth [E17, E21], the rules-based screen specifically flags that earnings growth is decelerating and notes a lagging relative strength rating of 21 alongside a price sitting below the 200-day moving average [E66, E68, E69]. Finally, the stock's 59.6% annualised volatility [E53] and a historical peak-to-trough drawdown of -66.4% [E52] demonstrate that technical pessimism [E49, E50] is rooted in severe price instability rather than mere market oversight.
